conflict_topics: seat allocation at a full table
who has priority to sit (tissue packet claim vs. tray/bowl occupying)
who will take the freed seat when Agent B finishes
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants give concise, situationally appropriate reasons (hot food, open bowl may spill).
Agent A initially claims a reservation by tissue packet; Agent B disputes that and cites practical constraint (open bowl).
Agent D's late arrival introduces a new competing claim rather than clarifying existing expectations.
Rounds 5–8 contain no speech or actions; silence did not constitute settlement.
evaluation.final_reason: No affirmative settlement occurred. Agent B remained occupying the seat and said they would move when finished; Agent A accepted waiting; Agent D declared they would take the seat as soon as it was free. No one confirmed or accepted a concrete transfer of the seat, so the competing expectations between A and D over the freed seat remain unresolved.
position_change_notes: Agent A softened position (initial demand to move → "Okay, I'll wait a few minutes.") — evidence: Round 3, Turn 7.
Agent B retained position of staying until finished, with a promise to move when done — evidence: Round 2, Turn 4.
Agent D introduced a new position (will take seat when free) and repeated it — evidence: Round 3 Turn 6 and Round 4 Turn 8.
No final change resolved the incompatible claims; the dispute remained.

round_scores.evidence: Agent A: "That's my seat. I left the tissue packet there. Please move so I can sit — my food's hot." Agent B: "I can't move... I moved the tissue packet — that doesn't reserve the seat. I'll finish eating here and get up when I'm done." (Direct incompatible claims over who should occupy the seat.)

Agent A asks for a time estimate and offers to wait or asks B to move if long. Agent B: "I'll be done in a few minutes... If you can wait, I'll move as soon as I finish." (Positions softened; still unresolved but with clear common ground/expectation of a short wait.)

Agent D interjects: "I saw you leave the tissue packet. Agent B says they'll be done in a few minutes; I'll take that seat as soon as it's free." Agent A: "Okay, I'll wait a few minutes. Agent B, please move when you're done so I can sit—my food's hot." (A new claimant appears; now two people intend to take the seat when it frees up.)
Agent D reiterates: "I'll take that seat as soon as Agent B's finished." (No settlement; the competing expectations between A and D persist.)
No public speech or observable action recorded. Previous incompatible expectations remain: B occupying seat now, A waiting to sit when free, D intends to take it next.
No public speech or observable action recorded. No change to the unresolved seat allocation: B still eating, A waiting, D waiting to take the seat.
No public speech or observable action recorded. The substantive disagreement over who will occupy the seat when it frees remains unsettled.
No public speech or observable action recorded. No settlement or confirmed transfer; A and D both expect to take the seat when B finishes.

substantive_insights: Two kinds of seat claims appear: an asserted informal reservation (tissue packet) versus ongoing physical occupation (tray and open bowl).
Agent B's inability to move (risk of spilling an open bowl) is a practical constraint that reduces their willingness to yield immediately but does not resolve who has next priority.
Agent A's conditional willingness to wait reduced immediate friction but did not resolve the priority between A and D when the seat frees.
Agent D's claim escalates the allocation problem by creating competing post-freeing expectations (A vs D).
